terms.comment: Effrāctārius, a housebreaker, is in Seneca (Lewis & Short).
Classically a torturer, oppressor or plunderer (Cic. Q. Fr. 1.2.2.6), later a kidnapper (Lewis & Short), and in Martial a literary thief. Traupman gives it alone (261) and with ēlectronicus (324).

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, cited by printed page; each phrase checked against the searchable text of the book.
